Title:117TH INTERNATIONAL OLYMPIC COMMITTEE SESSION (Economic costs and benefits)
MPs Speaking:Mdm Ho Geok Choo (West Coast);Miss Penny Low;Miss Penny Low (Pasir Ris-Punggol);Mr Ang Mong Seng (Hong Kah);The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)

Column: 1114

117TH INTERNATIONAL OLYMPIC COMMITTEE SESSION
(Economic costs and benefits)

      1.  Miss Penny Low asked the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports (a) what are the economic costs and benefits generated by the recent hosting of the International Olympic Committee in Singapore; and (b) how can we reap further benefits from the event.

     The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin

Column: 1115

Osman) (for the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports):  Mr Speaker, Sir, the 117th Session of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) that Singapore hosted recently was one of the biggest international sports meeting.  In fact, it has been described by some as the "next best thing to hosting the Olympic Games themselves".

 

     Singapore has benefited from hosting the event.  The Singapore Tourism Board had projected that it generated some S$40 million in economic spin-offs, including an estimated S$19 million in tourism receipts covering tourism-related industries such as retail, food and beverage, accommodation and recreation. This is a good return, considering that the expenditure incurred in organising the event was about S$7 million.
